messages:
samir: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a different approach for dashboard panel materialization. instead of full tiling, what if panels lazily materialize rows and only maintain small approx-counters for expensive aggregates?

jacob: short answer: love the idea for cost savings, but we need a clear materialization boundary. lazy + pushdown RBAC adds complexity in two places (query-layer & storage). how will we reason about correctness? :thinking:

priya: pushing RBAC predicates down to storage is key. if the storage can apply per-tenant ACL filters we avoid post-filtering large result sets. that reduces both CPU and memory at the frontend. downside: storage needs a tiny auth plugin or a token verifier.

liz: UX question — approximate counts are fine for dashboards but product wants exact on hover. we can keep fast approx for rendering and do an exact re-query for drilldowns. UX will need explicit affordance: "numbers are estimated".

jacob: implementation sketch: have a two-phase fetch for each panel: 1) lightweight head fetch (approx counts + top K keys, materialize prefixes) 2) on-interaction exact fetch. head fetch should be quorum-safe and use a single multiplexer path. example config: 
```
panel_config = {
  "materialization": "lazy",
  "head_fetch": {"approx_sample_rate": 0.02, "max_keys": 500},
  "rbac_pushdown": true,
  "exact_on_demand": true
}
```
This keeps normal renders cheap.

priya: operational tradeoffs: when head_fetch misses (cold) we must avoid thundering herd. require per-panel warm token + singleflight coalescing in the query multiplexer. also set a short soft-ttl for head caches so anomalies refresh quickly.

samir: what about query routing and SLOs? if head_fetch goes to cheaper replicas and exact fetches to stronger nodes, we must expose cost tiers in console routing policy. fallback: if exact node not available, surface approximate with an annotation.

liz: also consider RBAC edge cases: cross-tenant shared resources (projects visible to multiple teams) — pushdown needs to support boolean OR of multiple predicates. storage plugin must accept stable predicate tokens to avoid replay/privilege escalation.

jacob: agree. security checklist item: signed predicate tokens + short TTL + auditor trace. add to RFC follow-up.

ops-bot: deploy-check: canary for "panel-lazy-materialization" will be created after we land feature-flag. recommended rollout: 5% tenants for 48h, observe p50/p99 render latency and tokenized cost.

priya: measurable goals for canary: p50 render latency <= existing p50 * 1.1, token cost per panel <= 0.6x baseline, zero RBAC violations in audit logs.

samir: next steps I propose: (1) update the RFC with signed predicate token spec + storage plugin contract, (2) prototype head_fetch singleflight in the multiplexer, (3) wire UX toggle that labels approximate values. volunteers?

liz: I'll take the UX mock and copy for product.

jacob: I'll prototype the singleflight and default coalescing logic.

priya: I'll start the storage plugin spec and security review notes.

samir: great — I'll draft the RFC follow-up and add the rollout checklist. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
